newsitem.title: UK: Changes needed in LME rules - UBS lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Changes needed in LME rules - UBS lawyer.

text.p: Changes will have to be made in the way the London Metal Exchange (LME) operates but these need not be too radical, said Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) Ltd general counsel Mark Harding.

Harding told UBS clients they should respond to a questionnaire from Britain's lead financial regulator Securities and Investment Board (SIB) seeking trade and industry opinion on what, if any, changes should be made to the LME.

Until recently partner at law firm Clifford Chance dealing with futures markets, Hardy said changes are needed in the way the LME is governed as potential conflicts of interest often occur at board level where the majority are traders.

More reporting of trading activity is also needed. Hardy said that it may be feasible to increase reporting of large positions in LME contracts and address the problem of aggregating positions held by a single client with several brokers. But to also include positions held in the Over-the-Counter (OTC) market presented a greater problem.

The lawyer welcomed the move by U.S., UK and Japanese commodity futures regulators to cooperate more closely and share more information following the huge losses incurred by Sumitomo Corp in the copper market with the first meeting between these regulators takes place at the end of this month.
